name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute — Healthy Eating Recipes
note: Ingredients and nutrition as published by NHLBI (U.S. government). Steps are short summaries; each recipe links to the original.

recipes.title: 20-Minute Chicken Creole
recipes.desc: Quick Southern-style chicken in a spicy tomato sauce, made with no added fat.
ingredients: 12 oz boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into thin strips
1 cup canned whole peeled tomatoes, chopped
1 Tbsp fresh basil, chopped (or 1 tsp dried)
1 Tbsp fresh parsley, chopped (or 1 tsp dried)
steps: Coat a large skillet with cooking spray and heat it on high.
Cook the chicken strips for 3–5 minutes, stirring, then turn the heat down.
Stir in the tomatoes with their juice, chili sauce, green pepper, celery, onion, garlic, herbs, crushed red pepper and salt. Bring to a boil, then lower to a simmer.
Cover and simmer 10 minutes. Good over a small scoop of rice.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

recipes.title: Spicy Southern Barbecued Chicken
recipes.desc: Skinless chicken in a sweet-and-spicy homemade barbecue sauce, broiled then baked.
steps: Simmer everything except the chicken in a small saucepan for 15 minutes to make the sauce.
Brush the chicken with half the sauce, cover, and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Broil on a foil-lined sheet about 10 minutes per side.
Brush on the rest of the sauce, cover with foil and bake at 350°F for 30 minutes.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
source.book: Heart Healthy Home Cooking African American Style

recipes.title: New Orleans Red Beans
recipes.desc: Slow-simmered red beans with the Creole 'holy trinity' — creamy, with no meat or added fat.
steps: Pick over and rinse the beans.
Put the beans, water, onion, celery and bay leaves in a large pot, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer about 1½ hours until tender. Mash some beans against the pot.
Add the green pepper, garlic, parsley, thyme, salt and pepper and simmer uncovered about 30 minutes more until creamy. Remove the bay leaves.
Serve over brown rice if you like.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

recipes.title: Baked Fish
recipes.desc: Fish fillets in a seasoned cornflake crust, baked crisp instead of fried.
ingredients: ½ cup cornflakes, crumbled (or bread crumbs)
steps: Heat the oven to 475°F. Rub the fish with lemon juice and pat dry.
Stir together the buttermilk, hot sauce and garlic. Season the crushed cornflakes with the white pepper, salt and onion powder.
Dip each fillet in the buttermilk, then press into the crumbs on both sides. Let rest a few minutes so the coating sticks.
Bake on a lightly oiled dish on the middle rack for 20 minutes without turning. Serve with lemon wedges.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
source.book: Heart Healthy Home Cooking African American Style

recipes.title: Asian-Style Steamed Salmon
recipes.desc: Salmon gently poached in a ginger, shiitake and scallion broth.
recipes.servingSize: 3 oz salmon with ¼ cup broth
ingredients: ½ cup shiitake mushroom caps, sliced
2 Tbsp fresh minced ginger (or 2 tsp ground)
12 oz salmon fillet, cut into four 3-oz portions
steps: Bring the broth, mushrooms, ginger, scallions, soy sauce and optional sesame oil to a boil in a wide pan, then simmer 2–3 minutes.
Add the salmon, cover tightly and cook on low 4–5 minutes, until it flakes (145°F).
Serve each piece with a little of the broth, and rice if you like.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

recipes.title: Baked Salmon Dijon
recipes.desc: Salmon baked under a tangy dill, mustard and lemon topping.
ingredients: 1½ lb salmon fillet, cut into 6 portions
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Whisk the sour cream, dill, scallions, mustard and lemon juice.
Set the salmon skin-side down on a sprayed baking sheet, season with garlic powder and pepper, and spread the sauce on top.
Bake about 20 minutes, until the fish flakes (145°F).

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

recipes.title: Baked Tilapia With Tomatoes
recipes.desc: Tilapia baked under fresh tomatoes, olives, thyme and a little lime.
ingredients: ¼ cup pitted black olives, diced
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and spray a baking dish.
Lay the fillets in the dish without overlapping.
Mix the tomatoes, oil, thyme, olives, pepper flakes, garlic, onion and lime juice and spoon over the fish.
Bake uncovered 15–20 minutes until the fish flakes. Garnish with parsley and lemon.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

recipes.title: Braised Cod With Leeks
recipes.desc: Cod steamed on top of leeks, carrots and new potatoes in a light broth.
recipes.servingSize: 3 oz cod with 1½ cups vegetables and broth
ingredients: 2 cups leeks, thinly sliced and rinsed
3 medium carrots, cut into thin sticks
4 new (red) potatoes, sliced ½ inch thick
steps: Melt the butter in a wide pan and soften the leeks and carrots for 3–5 minutes.
Add the potatoes, broth, parsley, salt and pepper; boil, then simmer 10–12 minutes until just tender.
Lay the cod on top, cover tightly and cook on low about 5 minutes until it flakes (145°F).
Serve the fish with the vegetables and broth.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

recipes.title: Chicken Chile Stew
recipes.desc: Tender chicken slow-simmered with roasted green chilies, tomato and garlic.
ingredients: 7 green chilies, roasted, peeled, seeded and chopped
steps: Brown the chicken in batches in a sprayed heavy skillet.
Move it to a covered pot with the celery, tomato, chilies and garlic.
Add a splash of water to the skillet, scrape up the browned bits and pour into the pot. Add water to barely cover.
Cover and simmer about 1½ hours until thick and very tender. Season with pepper.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
source.book: Honoring the Gift of Heart Health

recipes.title: Chicken Picadillo
recipes.desc: Latin-style chicken with peppers, tomato, cumin, raisins, capers and olives.
ingredients: 1 medium green bell pepper, finely chopped
1 medium red bell pepper, finely chopped
12 oz boneless, skinless chicken breast, thin strips
Garnish: 1 Tbsp cilantro, 1 Tbsp capers, 2 Tbsp chopped green olives
steps: Soften the onion, peppers and garlic in the oil, about 5 minutes.
Add the chicken and cook 5–10 minutes until no longer pink.
Stir in the tomato sauce, broth, lemon juice, cumin, bay leaves, water and raisins. Cover and simmer 10 minutes.
Remove the bay leaves and top with cilantro, capers and olives.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

recipes.title: Hawaiian Huli Huli Chicken
recipes.desc: Chicken and pineapple skewers glazed with a light ginger-soy sauce.
ingredients: 12 oz boneless, skinless chicken breast, 1-inch cubes
1 cup fresh pineapple chunks (or canned in juice)
steps: Heat a grill or broiler to medium-high.
Thread chicken and pineapple onto the skewers, three of each per skewer.
Mix the sauce and split it into two bowls — one for basting, one for serving.
Grill 3–5 minutes per side, basting every other minute. Throw away the basting sauce.
Finish in a 350°F oven until the chicken reaches 165°F. Brush with the clean sauce to serve.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

recipes.title: Marinated Chicken (Adobong Manok)
recipes.desc: A lighter Filipino adobo — chicken braised in vinegar, garlic and pepper, then broiled.
steps: Brown the chicken with the oil, garlic and onion.
Add the soy sauce, vinegar, paprika, pepper and bay leaf, bring to a boil, then simmer 45–60 minutes until done.
Lift out the chicken and broil it until browned.
Boil the pan sauce until reduced by half, pour over the chicken and add tomato wedges if you like.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

recipes.title: Grilled Tuna With Chickpea and Spinach Salad
recipes.desc: Lemon-oregano tuna steaks over a fresh spinach, chickpea and tomato salad.
ingredients: 12 oz tuna steak, cut into 4 portions
Salad: ½ can (15½ oz) low-sodium chickpeas, rinsed
steps: Heat a grill pan or broiler on high.
Mix the oil, garlic, lemon juice and oregano, brush over the tuna and let it sit 5–10 minutes.
Toss the salad ingredients together (can be made 2 hours ahead).
Grill or broil the tuna 3–4 minutes per side (145°F) and serve over the salad.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

recipes.title: Turkey Bolognese With Shell Pasta
recipes.desc: Lean turkey simmered with vegetables and tomato, seasoned with anise for an Italian-sausage taste.
steps: If using, simmer the wine with the dried mushrooms for 20 minutes.
Finely chop the onion, celery, carrots and garlic. Put pasta water on to boil.
Brown the turkey in the oil with the anise seed and salt, 5–10 minutes. Cook the pasta.
Add the vegetables and cook 10 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste and simmer 5–10 minutes. Add the wine and chopped mushrooms if using.
Toss with the drained pasta and top each plate with 2 Tbsp Parmesan.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

recipes.title: Red Beans and Rice
recipes.desc: A fast Cajun classic with kidney beans, peppers, cumin and brown rice — ready in 30 minutes.
ingredients: 1 can (14½ oz) low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth
2 cans (15 oz) low-sodium red kidney beans, rinsed
steps: Soften the onion in the oil about 5 minutes.
Add the pepper, cover and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, cumin and oregano for 1 minute.
Add the broth and rice, cover and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the rinsed beans and simmer 5 minutes more. Good with steamed broccoli.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

recipes.title: Turkey Club Burger
recipes.desc: A lean turkey burger on whole wheat with greens and a light Dijon spread.
ingredients: 4 oz portabella mushroom, grilled and sliced (optional)
steps: Heat the broiler or grill.
Mix the turkey, scallions, pepper and egg, shape 4 patties and brush lightly with oil.
Cook 7–9 minutes per side to 160°F.
Stir the mayonnaise and mustard together, and build each burger with spread, greens and mushroom.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

recipes.title: Minestrone Soup
recipes.desc: A big pot of classic Italian vegetable soup with beans, peas and a little pasta.
ingredients: 1 can (15½ oz) low-sodium red kidney beans, rinsed
steps: Warm the oil in a large pot and cook the garlic, onion and celery about 5 minutes.
Add everything else except the spaghetti, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer about 45 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the broken spaghetti for the last 2–3 minutes only.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

recipes.title: Lentil Soup
recipes.desc: Hearty lentils simmered with carrots, celery, tomato and herbs — even better the next day.
steps: Cook the carrots, celery and onion in the oil until the onion is tender.
Add the garlic, oregano, basil and pepper for 2 minutes.
Add the lentils, tomatoes, broth and water, cover and bring to a boil, then simmer at least 1 hour until the lentils are soft.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

recipes.title: Mushroom Penne
recipes.desc: Whole-wheat penne with mushrooms, thyme and a splash of red wine.
steps: Boil the pasta for the shortest time on the package.
Brown the mushrooms in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the onion and garlic for 3 minutes.
Add the wine and scrape up the browned bits, then the broth, salt, pepper and thyme.
Stir in the drained pasta and simmer about 3 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Top each serving with 1 Tbsp Parmesan.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

recipes.title: Chicken and Mushroom Fricassee
recipes.desc: Chicken legs braised with mushrooms, leeks and potatoes in a light herb sauce.
recipes.servingSize: 1 chicken leg, 1 cup vegetables and sauce
ingredients: 1 lb skinless chicken legs or thighs
2 Tbsp each fresh parsley and chives
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Brown the mushrooms in the oil in an ovenproof pan, then soften the leeks, potatoes, celery and onions.
Add the broth, bring to a boil, add the chicken, cover and bake about 20 minutes (165°F).
Lift out the chicken, boil the liquid on the stove and add the herbs and lemon.
Stir the cornstarch into the sour cream, whisk into the pan, bring back to a boil and season. Spoon over the chicken.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

recipes.title: Heavenly Chicken With Angel Hair Pasta
recipes.desc: Chicken and broccoli in a mildly spicy tomato sauce over whole-wheat angel hair.
ingredients: 8 oz thin-sliced chicken breast, ½-inch strips
steps: Put pasta water on to boil.
Brown the chicken in the hot oil, 5–8 minutes, and set aside.
Spray the pan, cook the onion 3 minutes, then the garlic and broccoli 2 minutes.
Return the chicken with the sauce, cayenne and salt; cover and simmer about 4 minutes.
Cook the angel hair about 2 minutes, drain and top with the chicken and sauce.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

recipes.title: Homemade Turkey Soup
recipes.desc: From-scratch soup from a leftover turkey, with herbs and small pasta.
ingredients: 1 turkey carcass with at least 2 cups meat left on
½ lb pastina or other small pasta
steps: Cover the carcass with water in a 6-quart pot, add the onions and celery, and simmer covered about 2½ hours.
Lift out the carcass. Chill the broth in shallow containers and pick the meat off the bones.
Skim the fat from the chilled broth and return it to the pot with the meat and herbs.
Bring to a boil, add the pasta and cook about 20 minutes on a low boil.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

recipes.title: Vegetable Stew
recipes.desc: Potatoes, carrots, squash and corn in a thick, lightly spiced broth.
ingredients: 1 cup summer squash, in 4 large chunks
1 can (15 oz) sweet corn, rinsed (or 2 ears fresh)
steps: Bring the water and bouillon to a boil, add the potatoes and carrots and simmer 5 minutes.
Add everything except the tomatoes and cook 15 minutes.
Purée the four big squash chunks and stir them back in to thicken; cook 10 minutes.
Add the tomatoes for 5 minutes, then let stand 10 minutes before serving.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
source.book: Heart Healthy Home Cooking African American Style

recipes.title: Turkey and Beef Meatballs With Whole-Wheat Spaghetti
recipes.desc: Baked lean meatballs over whole-wheat spaghetti — a family favorite made lighter.
recipes.servingSize: 4 meatballs, ¾ cup pasta, ½ cup sauce
ingredients: Turkey meatballs: 6 oz 99% lean ground turkey, ¼ cup whole-wheat breadcrumbs, 2 Tbsp fat-free evaporated milk, 1 Tbsp Parmesan, ½ Tbsp each chives and parsley
Beef meatballs: 6 oz 93% lean ground beef, ¼ cup whole-wheat breadcrumbs, 2 Tbsp fat-free evaporated milk, 1 Tbsp Parmesan, ½ Tbsp each chives and parsley
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and cook the spaghetti.
Mix each meatball set in its own bowl and roll into 8 balls of each (about 1½ Tbsp).
Bake 10 minutes on a nonstick sheet, to 165°F.
Serve 4 meatballs with pasta, warm sauce, a teaspoon of cheese and basil.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

recipes.title: Fresh Lumpia (Lumpiang Sariwa)
recipes.desc: Filipino fresh spring rolls filled with chicken, shrimp and crisp vegetables.
ingredients: ½ cup ground chicken breast or lean pork
½ cup each cabbage, green beans and carrots, julienned
¼ cup each celery and jicama, julienned
Sauce: 1 cup reserved broth, 1 Tbsp lite soy sauce, 1 Tbsp brown sugar, 3 cloves garlic, 1 tsp cornstarch
steps: Sauté the meat, shrimp and garlic, add the vegetables until just crisp, then the broth; season.
Strain, keeping the broth, and let the filling cool.
Simmer 1 cup broth with the soy sauce, sugar and garlic and thicken with the cornstarch mixed in a little cold water.
Soften each wrapper, add a lettuce leaf and 2 Tbsp filling, and roll up. Top with sauce and peanuts.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

recipes.title: Vietnamese Fresh Spring Rolls (Gỏi Cuốn)
recipes.desc: Crisp vegetables and fresh herbs rolled in rice paper — no cooking needed.
steps: Toss the vegetables and herbs together.
Soften a rice paper in warm water 1–2 minutes and shake off the water.
Add some filling, fold in the sides and roll up tightly. Repeat, and serve right away.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

recipes.title: Caribbean Pink Beans
recipes.desc: Pink beans simmered with plantains, tomato and pepper — no lard or added fat.
ingredients: 1 small red bell pepper, finely chopped
steps: Soak the rinsed beans overnight in the fridge in 10 cups of water.
Drain, cover with fresh water by an inch, and simmer with the lid ajar about 1 hour until soft.
Add the plantains, tomato, pepper, onion, garlic and salt and cook on low until the plantains are soft.

source.name: NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
